subject: ela
intro: Fifth graders integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably. Combining facts from multiple sources gives a fuller, more accurate understanding than one source alone, and lets you check that facts agree.

items.prompt:
Text A: 'Sharks are fish.' Text B: 'Sharks have skeletons made of cartilage, not bone.' Text C: 'Some sharks can smell a drop of blood from far away.'

Using all three, describe sharks.

steps: I combine the key facts from each text.
A: fish; B: cartilage skeleton; C: strong sense of smell.
So sharks are fish with cartilage skeletons and a powerful sense of smell.
solution.answer: Sharks are fish with cartilage skeletons and a powerful sense of smell.

items.prompt:
Two of the three texts above state that sharks are fish.

What does this agreement tell you?

steps: When sources agree, you can trust the fact more.
So you can be more confident sharks are fish.
solution.answer: You can be more confident that fact is correct.

items.prompt: Why is reading SEVERAL texts better than one for a report?

steps: Each text adds facts and lets you check others.
So you get a fuller, more reliable report.
solution.answer: You get more facts and can check that they agree.

items.prompt: Combining facts from several texts gives a ____ understanding.
When sources agree on a fact, you can ____ it more.
